content.user_title: Build Drug Discovery Models with TorchDrug
content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need structured guidance for TorchDrug models, datasets, and workflows. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan molecular, protein, knowledge graph, generation, and retrosynthesis tasks.
actual_capabilities: Maps drug discovery tasks to TorchDrug workflows and reference files.
Guides dataset selection for molecular, protein, knowledge graph, and retrosynthesis work.
Compares model families including GIN, GAT, SchNet, GearNet, ESM, RotatE, and ComplEx.
Explains training patterns for property prediction, protein modeling, knowledge graph completion, generation, and retrosynthesis.
Provides integration guidance for RDKit, AlphaFold structures, ESM models, and PyTorch Lightning.
Helps troubleshoot dimension mismatches, weak performance, memory issues, and invalid generated molecules.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not install TorchDrug or run experiments by itself.
Results depend on local datasets, GPU resources, package versions, and chemistry validation tools.
It does not replace medicinal chemistry review, regulatory review, or experimental validation.
Generated molecules and synthesis routes require independent validity, safety, and feasibility checks.

use_cases.title: Plan Molecular Property Prediction
use_cases.description: Select datasets, graph models, metrics, and split strategies for ADMET or toxicity prediction tasks.

use_cases.title: Compare Protein Modeling Options
use_cases.description: Choose sequence or structure models for enzyme function, protein stability, or localization prediction.

use_cases.title: Design Discovery Workflows
use_cases.description: Connect molecular generation, knowledge graph reasoning, and retrosynthesis guidance for candidate discovery.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first TorchDrug task.
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to use TorchDrug for a drug discovery task. Ask me the key questions, then recommend a dataset, model family, task type, and evaluation metric.

prompt_templates.title: Select Models and Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare TorchDrug options for my task: [describe task]. Recommend suitable datasets, model architectures, split strategy, metrics, and likely pitfalls.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Training Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: User preparing an experiment before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TorchDrug training plan for correctness: [paste plan]. Check data leakage, feature dimensions, model-task fit, metrics, and validation strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user combining multiple discovery stages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TorchDrug pipeline that combines property prediction, knowledge graph reasoning, molecular generation, and retrosynthesis. Include validation gates and failure checks.

output_examples.input: I need to predict blood-brain barrier penetration for candidate molecules.
output_examples.output: Recommended path: use the BBBP dataset, start with a GIN molecular graph model, use scaffold splitting, and evaluate AUROC plus AUPRC.

output_examples.input: My generated molecules are often invalid.
output_examples.output: Suggested checks: add validity constraints, use RDKit post-processing, penalize invalid structures in rewards, and track uniqueness, novelty, and diversity.

output_examples.input: I want to use Hetionet for drug repurposing.
output_examples.output: Recommended path: use knowledge graph completion, compare RotatE and ComplEx, train with negative sampling, and filter compound-disease predictions by mechanism.

best_practices: Start with the reference file that matches the task before choosing a model.
Use scaffold splits for molecular prediction when generalization to new scaffolds matters.
Validate generated molecules, predicted reactions, and biological links outside the model.
anti_patterns: Do not use random splits for molecular tasks when scaffold leakage changes the result.
Do not choose a model before confirming dataset features and task output shape.
Do not treat generated compounds or retrosynthesis routes as experimentally verified outputs.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps plan TorchDrug workflows for molecules, proteins, biomedical knowledge graphs, generation, retrosynthesis, and graph neural networks.

faq.question: Does it run TorchDrug experiments?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users still run code, manage packages, and validate outputs in their own environment.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help choose a dataset?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers molecular, protein, knowledge graph, and retrosynthesis datasets, including task types and selection criteria.

faq.question: Can it help with model selection?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares TorchDrug model families for graph, protein, knowledge graph, and generative tasks.

faq.question: Is it suitable for validated drug design decisions?
faq.answer: No. It supports research planning only. Chemistry, biology, safety, and regulatory conclusions need expert validation.
